questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was a bigger city within Europe

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was a good amount of information from the Erasmus University Rotterdam, could have used a bit more e.g. a follow up on the insurance rules, which never came. The administration was quick to answer whenever I had a question and was very flexible.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None, beside an e-mail to state which date and place the introduction would be held.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Almost all other faculties at the university, beside law, had two full introduction days, days in the middle of exchange and at the end of exchange to catch up with the exchange students and give them an oppotunity to meet each other. However, for some reason, nothing was arranged for the law students. You were pretty much on your own after the short introduction to the university.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The university did a great job presenting a realistic picture of the housing crisis that is currently affecting the country and making the exchange students aware of this.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You were able to buy food and eat food at campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The ability to live on campus makes your exchange much easier and more straightforward, for example in regards to not having to worry about being scammed by landlords if you were to rent on the private market. So definitely priotize housing provided through the university if in anyway possible! However, you should be aware that on-campus living seemed very limited compared to how many exchange students there was.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are many more exchange students than there is housing provided through the university. This means that if you are not lucky to get something through the university, it will require a much bigger effort to find housing elsewhere.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The administration was pretty good at to continuously inform the students about what the next steps for the registration process would be in terms of courses and so on. However the exam board and the administration was very unclear when it came to anything else than that. I did, for example, ask whether a re-sit would be possible in my homecountry. The exam board stopped answering my e-mail in the middle of the correspondance, and then randomly mailed me that I was granted the permission for a re-sit. Firstly, they didn't tell me the fact that they were processing my request and secondly, the decision they granted me in the end had nothing to do with what I originally asked for (if I was still at in the country at the time the re-sit was, I would have just signed up for that one). Thirdly, it took them two months to grant the desicion, which had the requirement that the re-sit must be held before the end of august. Since I wasn't been informed that they were processing a decision, I had no clue that I might had needed to clear my calendar for August (getting the permission granted three weeks before the end of august). That was unfortunately not a good experience.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Call or e-mail to the university's administration for international students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There was no problems with the registration for classes. They were also very flexible in terms of letting people switch to other classes (even though the classes had already started or would start in only a few days)

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To just ask the university if e.g. you want to change from one course to another, since they were very flexible with that.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level was pretty high and the written exam was challenging since you couldn't bring any notes or books. Also, you should be aware that if you arrive

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: You should also be aware that if you arrive in the spring semester, you will start taking courses that are in the middle of the academic year for permanent students, which can be a bit confusing.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty much the same, beside the fact that the university had much more guest lectures and trips out of the university than UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Maritime Casualties, Intellectual Property law, EU Competition law, International Health Law and Carriage of Goods

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Carriage of Goods and EU Competition law

questions.answer: A on-campus fitness center.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: None arranged through the university

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to different cities in Holland or go to places with techno-music. Go see an art gallery or go to the lake.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If anyone invites you to something, go!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Lots of different ways to experience the country

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the housing crisis situation, try and connect with the other exchange student (e.g. make a whatsapp group or something) on the intro-day, since it makes it easier to meet up, since there wasn't any other social events through the university.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of international students at the university (beside from exchange students), so the Unviersity also felt very international in general and people would in general speak english as default.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To live a very international city, while being able to be tourists with your friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: There would be exams every other month, since the exams was divided in blocks, which could be a bit stressful.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
